Anya (CS): dropping a tiny customer-facing warmup/runbook for fast onboard -> reduce renewal friction. single-page, rep-friendly.
Marco (CS Ops): please include a 3-question decision check for sales. keep it binary.
Anya (CS): decision checks: 1) chat-like UX? 2) >30 expected first-24h sessions? 3) ok with small warmup token spend? recommend warmup if 2+ yes.
Ravi (Eng): runtime-safe defaults (copyable YAML):
Ravi (Eng): ```yaml
warmup:
  enabled: true
  minutes: 30
  concurrency: 3
cache:
  edge_ttl_s: 60
  kv_ttl_min: 20
batching:
  max_tokens: 1024
  hold_ms: 20
streaming:
  prefer: true
  fallback: single_shot
```
Sam (SRE): monitoring quicklines: synthetic prefill probe every 3m; page if p95 >400ms for 10m or error_rate >1.5%. log warmup tokens and tag ticket when >0.5% monthly budget.
Anya (CS): rep email snippet: "Subject: Quick warmup before launch
Hi <Name>, we plan a short warmup to improve first-hour latency and UX. It warms a small pool and caches examples for ~1h. Reply to opt out.
Thanks, <rep>"
Marco (CS Ops): ticket fields to add: prefill_consent: yes/no and prefill_notes. reps capture objections (cost/privacy) and next steps.
Anya (CS): renewal trigger suggestion: <4 meaningful sessions in 24h AND p95 >250ms for >12h -> auto-flag for outreach; flagged twice in 7 days -> schedule health call.
